header.provenance: own-binary-via-Ghidra (entry points) + objdump -d -M intel (instruction stream, same file)
header.status: leads — every record is read straight off the instruction stream; confirm against the disassembly before it enters a header
header.what_this_is: RET n is callee stack cleanup, so the immediate is ground truth for how many argument bytes the callee removed. Whether ECX/EDX are read before being written says whether they carried a receiver and a register argument. Together they pin the calling convention before a line of C++ is written.
inference_rules: ECX read before write, EDX not, RET n -> __thiscall; n = stack argument bytes.

ECX and EDX both read before write, RET n -> __fastcall; n counts only the REMAINING arguments. This may be a free __fastcall or a __fastcall member; the census cannot distinguish those and does not pretend to.
neither read before write, RET n -> __stdcall; n = stack argument bytes.
neither read before write, bare RET -> __cdecl, OR a __stdcall/__thiscall with no stack arguments. AMBIGUOUS, marked confidence=ambiguous.

excluded_kinds.tail-jump: terminates in JMP, not RET; the convention belongs to the jump target (follow tail_jump_targets)
excluded_kinds.no-ret: no RET reached: noreturn, or a function-boundary error
excluded_kinds.conflicting-ret: several RETs disagree on the immediate; read by hand

caveats: A RET inside a __try region, or after a stack-cleanup thunk, can mislead; such functions are not separately flagged here.
reads_ecx/edx_before_write is computed over the CFG from the entry point, with ECX and EDX treated as clobbered by any CALL.
__fastcall vs __thiscall is decided by EDX, not by argument count. See docs/matching_methodology_and_toolchain.md batch fifty.

A __thiscall verdict says ECX carried a receiver-shaped value; it does not prove the function is a non-static member (it may be a static __fastcall member or a free __fastcall whose second parameter is unused).

field_notes.ret_imm: the single distinct terminating RET immediate, or the LIST of distinct immediates when the returns disagree (conflicting_returns=true). 0 means a bare RET.
field_notes.ret_imms: every distinct terminating RET immediate reached from the entry.
field_notes.confidence: high | ambiguous (bare RET, convention underdetermined) | excluded (not a data point: see excluded_kinds).
field_notes.entry_point_is_lead: true when the entry point itself came from a sweep rather than Ghidra's function list, so the boundary is unconfirmed even where the convention reads cleanly.
field_notes.seh_frame: the prologue installs an SEH handler; a RET inside a __try region can mislead, so read this one by hand.
